subject: Using Rasch estimates for single-indicator SEM

messages.author: f9a02a1a390eea1a
messages.subject: Using Rasch estimates for single-indicator SEM
parts:
Hi,

I have a question similar to https://groups.google.com/g/lavaan/c/e9kXRtiL9lU/m/UDhKy0XVRhIJ
but relating more to how to constrain variances of endogenous latent variables.

I have a model consisting of 5 latent variables each measured by a single indicator, the indicators are themselves the result of Rasch analyses of a particular questionnaires. I know I can use the reliability (PSI) of each indicator derived from the Rasch model to specify error variances, indicator loadings and latent variances that satisfy var(x)=loading^2 * var(f) + err_var(x).
 eg.

x1 ~~ 3.5*x1 (fix measurement error variance of indicator x1)
f1 =~ 2.8*x1 (fix loading of factor f1 onto indicator x1)

but I also want to pre-fix the latent variances.  My questions are:
(1) What does the syntax
f1 ~~ 0.5*f
do? I think this fixes the residual variance of the latent factor, event though I want to fix the total variance of each latent factor (var(f)). Can I fix the total variance?

(2) How are the exogenous and endogenous latent variances treated by lavaan? In the output "Variances" list, I think we just assume that exogenous ones are total variances and endogenous ones are disturbances. Is this right? If I set std.lv=TRUE, does this relate to total or residual variances being set to 1? Are they standardised differently to each other?

Perhaps these are very obvious questions, sorry. I cannot find any evidence that suggests using these Rasch estimates is OK for endogenous variables - perhaps because I cannot specify the latent variances. I'm tying my head in knots trying to understand - would really appreciate some clarity!

Thanks,

Rebecca

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Using Rasch estimates for single-indicator SEM
parts:
What does the syntax
f1 ~~ 0.5*f
do? I think this fixes the residual variance of the latent factor
Can I fix the total variance?
No, that is not a model parameter (except coincidentally: an exogenous factor's residual variance is its total variance).

(2) How are the exogenous and endogenous latent variances treated by lavaan? In the output "Variances" list, I think we just assume that exogenous ones are total variances and endogenous ones are disturbances. Is this right?
Yes, or as I pointed out above, the disturbance of an exogenous factor could be seen merely as the factor itself.
If I set std.lv=TRUE, does this relate to total or residual variances being set to 1?

The latter.  Total variances are not model parameters (except by coincidence).
